title: plugin-auth: admin/set-user-manager refuses every user who has signed in through SSO as "directory-owned", even where no directory exists, so on a hosted environment nobody's manager can be changed after their first sign-in
body:
domain:server#7 · os-tesla · session_01L9qibzuZJBQY4wUQFJbkfx

Filing gate: ① a public door gives a wrong answer, class a. Found during the #33181 measurement. ⛔ Not a claim; triage sets the lane and grade.

## What happens

`POST /api/v1/auth/admin/set-user-manager` refuses a target whose `sys_user.source` is `idp_provisioned` with `403 PERMISSION_DENIED`: "This identity is provisioned by an external directory (sys_user.source is 'idp_provisioned'), so its manager is maintained by that directory and a value written here would be reverted on the next sync. Set the manager in the directory instead." (`admin-set-user-manager.ts` ~L514).

`idp_provisioned` is not a directory mark. ADR-0135 D4 stamps it on any federated link without a local password (`stampIdentitySource`, `auth-manager-database-hooks.ts` ~L597), so the cloud's own platform SSO (`objectstack-cloud`) stamps it on every person's first sign-in to a hosted environment, and a social or enterprise OIDC sign-in stamps it too. On those rows there is no directory, no sync and no place where the manager could be set "instead".

## Repro (reach: public door, wrong answer)

Measured at objectstack-ai/objectstack `origin/main` 88355328, a real `AuthManager` behind `AuthPlugin.registerAuthRoutes` on Hono, caller a platform administrator:
- target `source: idp_provisioned`, no `sys_scim_subject` row (no SCIM directory), no local credential (what a platform-SSO first sign-in leaves): `403 PERMISSION_DENIED` with the sentence above; `manager_id` not written. Same on a cloud-managed environment and on a self-hosted one.
- CONTROL: the same call on an `env_native` target answers 200.

Consequence on a hosted Free/Team environment (no SCIM): a manager can be set while a person is not yet signed in, and never again once they have signed in, so approval flows that route by manager cannot follow a reorganisation.

## Seam

`Seam: platform-objects:sys_user.source (idp_provisioned) → runtime: admin-set-user-manager.ts applyUserManagerLink directory-owned refusal`. The ruling that made it (5651634638 row 7, "directory wins") is about a SCIM directory; the predicate reads a mark that also covers SSO-only users. A narrower predicate (a `sys_scim_subject` row, the condition `scim-sso-adoption.ts` uses for "held by a SCIM directory") is the likely fix; the ruling's scope is the maintainer's to confirm.

Dedupe words: `set-user-manager idp_provisioned`, `directory-owned manager`, `manager reverted on the next sync`, `applyUserManagerLink`.
